gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: Who will ___ responsibility for the project now that Jane has left?
gaps.explanation: take responsibility for something means to accept the duty of dealing with it.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.

gaps.sentence: Local residents are deeply ___ about the new motorway plan.
gaps.explanation: deeply concerned is the standard collocation meaning very worried; the other adjectives do not collocate with 'deeply'.

gaps.sentence: The wedding will ___ place in the village church.
gaps.explanation: take place means to happen; it is the fixed phrase for events.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: I'm ___ a course in web design this term.
gaps.explanation: do a course is the British English collocation for studying on a course.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.
